claim: The survey of prompt engineering by R1 describes it as a technique that uses task-specific instructions to enhance model efficacy without modifying core model parameters.
quote: Prompt engineering has emerged as an indispensable technique for extending the capabilities of large language models (LLMs) and vision-language models (VLMs). This approach leverages task-specific instructions, known as prompts, to enhance model efficacy without modifying the core model parameters.

claim: The abstract of R11 states that prompts are also a form of programming that can customize the outputs and interactions with an LLM.
quote: Prompts are also a form of programming that can customize the outputs and interactions with an LLM.

claim: The authors of R2 report that prompt engineering is frequently treated as an empirical, ad hoc practice lacking a standardized theoretical framework.
quote: Despite the critical role of prompt engineering, it is frequently treated as an empirical, ad hoc practice lacking a standardized theoretical framework, leading to challenges such as output inconsistency, prompt sensitivity, and hallucinations.

claim: The same survey frames its analysis around a shift from input-level linguistic control to system-level contextual orchestration.
quote: By analyzing the shift from input-level linguistic control to system-level contextual orchestration, we identify persistent limitations, such as context dilution and computational overhead.

claim: R1 describes retrieval-augmented generation as emerging as a novel solution that seamlessly weaves information retrieval into the prompting process.
quote: Retrieval Augmented Generation (RAG) [Lewis et al., 2020] emerges as a novel solution, seamlessly weaving information retrieval into the prompting process.

claim: The Agentic RAG survey R17 states that agents leverage reflection, planning, tool use, and multi-agent collaboration to manage retrieval strategies.
quote: Agentic Retrieval-Augmented Generation (Agentic RAG) transcends these limitations by embedding autonomous AI agents into the RAG pipeline. These agents leverage agentic design patterns reflection, planning, tool use, and multi-agent collaboration to dynamically manage retrieval strategies, iteratively refine contextual understanding, and adapt workflows through operational structures ranging from sequential steps to adaptive collaboration.

claim: The authors of R24 implement memory not as a vector database, but as a persistent file system accessible via tool calls.
quote: we implement M not as a vector database, but as a persistent file system accessible via tool calls.

claim: The study R18 notes that agents on long-running tasks inevitably exceed their usable context window, forcing a choice about what history to discard.
quote: Large language model (LLM) agents operating on long-running tasks inevitably exceed their usable context window, forcing a choice about what history to discard.

claim: The paper R20 describes context rot as the progressive and nonlinear degradation of agent reasoning quality and tool calling reliability as the context window fills.
quote: a phenomenon now termed context rot has emerged: the progressive and nonlinear degradation of agent reasoning quality and tool calling reliability as the context window fills during extended coding sessions.

claim: The authors of R6 state that changing the execution system around a fixed model can alter performance and even reverse model rankings.
quote: recent results highlight the importance of the agent harness: changing the execution system around a fixed model can alter performance and even reverse model rankings.

claim: The authors of R26 define scaling the harness as treating the structured execution layer around a foundation model as a first-class object of design, evaluation, and optimization.
quote: We refer to this shift as scaling the harness: treating the structured execution layer around a foundation model as a first-class object of design, evaluation, and optimization.

claim: The survey R8 takes the agent loop, rather than the model in isolation, as its unit of analysis.
quote: Every LLM agent, beneath its framework and its prompts, runs a loop: it observes, decides, acts, and observes again until it stops. This survey takes that agent loop, not the model in isolation, as its unit of analysis, on the argument that the properties practitioners actually care about, cost, reliability, and safety, are decided by the loop rather than by the model alone.

claim: A survey of prompt and context engineering analyses the shift from input-level linguistic control to system-level contextual orchestration and names context dilution and computational overhead as persistent limitations.
quote: By analyzing the shift from input-level linguistic control to system-level contextual orchestration, we identify persistent limitations, such as context dilution and computational overhead.

claim: The ACE paper describes LLM applications as increasingly relying on context adaptation, meaning the modification of inputs with instructions, strategies, or evidence rather than weight updates.
quote: Large language model (LLM) applications such as agents and domain-specific reasoning increasingly rely on context adaptation: modifying inputs with instructions, strategies, or evidence, rather than weight updates.

claim: The ACE authors report that it optimizes contexts both offline (e.g., system prompts) and online (e.g., agent memory), outperforming strong baselines by +10.6% on agents and +8.6% on finance.
quote: Across agent and domain-specific benchmarks, ACE optimizes contexts both offline (e.g., system prompts) and online (e.g., agent memory), consistently outperforming strong baselines: +10.6% on agents and +8.6% on finance, while significantly reducing adaptation latency and rollout cost.

claim: The Code as Agent Harness survey distinguishes prompt engineering as changing instructions and context engineering as changing what evidence is presented to the model, while Agentic Harness Engineering treats the operating environment itself as the object of analysis.
quote: Whereas prompt engineering changes instructions and context engineering changes what evidence is presented to the model, AHE treats the operating environment itself as the object of analysis, including tool schemas, planning artifacts, memory policies, retrieval strategies, sandbox configuration, verification sensors, permission tiers, routing rules, multiagent workflows, and human-review gates [281,178].
locator: sec. Agentic Harness Engineering for Adaptive Harness Optimization, para 96

claim: The scaling-the-harness paper lists a context constructor as one of six interacting components alongside a memory store, skill routing, an orchestration loop, and a governance layer.
quote: Under this view, an agent is not simply a model with a prompt, but a system composed of six interacting components: a reasoning substrate (R), a memory store (M), a context constructor (C), a skill-routing layer (S, which dispatches tools and subagents), an orchestration loop (O), and a verification and governance layer (G).

claim: One study states that context rot manifests well before nominal token limits are reached, as tool schema definitions consume a disproportionate share of the context budget and model attention weakens for information deep within growing prompts.
quote: Context rot manifests well before nominal token limits are reached, as tool schema definitions consume a disproportionate share of the available context budget and model attention weakens for information positioned deep within growing prompts.

claim: Another reports that, in calibrated simulation over the Agentic Context Benchmark (ACB-2026), Skills Architecture reduced normalized context entropy by 42% relative to baseline MCP.
quote: In controlled experiments using calibrated simulation over the Agentic Context Benchmark (ACB-2026), Skills Architecture reduces normalized context entropy by 42% (95% CI: [37%, 46%]) relative to baseline MCP

claim: The harness survey R29 describes the agent harness as the external execution support structure built around the model and treats it as a distinct performance lever.
quote: We understand the agent harness as the external execution support structure built around the model and treat it as a distinct performance lever that complements base model capability

claim: The scaling-the-harness paper names six interacting components: a reasoning substrate, a memory store, a context constructor, a skill-routing layer, an orchestration loop, and a verification and governance layer.
quote: a system composed of six interacting components: a reasoning substrate (R), a memory store (M), a context constructor (C), a skill-routing layer (S, which dispatches tools and subagents), an orchestration loop (O), and a verification and governance layer (G)

claim: The externalization review assigns roles differently: memory externalizes state across time, skills externalize procedural expertise, protocols externalize interaction structure, and the harness unifies them into governed execution.
quote: memory externalizes state across time, skills externalize procedural expertise, protocols externalize interaction structure, and harness engineering serves as the unification layer that coordinates them into governed execution

claim: R29 describes a shifting boundary in which routine capability-bearing support migrates into model weights while constraint-bearing governance functions remain external.
quote: explaining the shifting functional boundary where routine capability-bearing support migrates inward into model weights while constraint-bearing governance functions remain external

claim: The Agent Loop survey states that every LLM agent, beneath its framework and prompts, runs a loop in which it observes, decides, acts, and observes again until it stops.
quote: Every LLM agent, beneath its framework and its prompts, runs a loop: it observes, decides, acts, and observes again until it stops.

claim: The same survey theorises that the loop is being internalized into weights and externalized into skills and harnesses.
quote: One thesis runs throughout: the loop is being pulled in two directions at once, internalized into weights and externalized into skills and harnesses.

claim: The scaling-the-harness paper names six components of an agent: a reasoning substrate, memory store, context constructor, skill-routing layer, orchestration loop, and verification and governance layer.
quote: Under this view, an agent is not simply a model with a prompt, but a system composed of six interacting components: a reasoning substrate (R), a memory store (M), a context constructor (C), a skill-routing layer (S, which dispatches tools and subagents), an orchestration loop (O), and a verification and governance layer (G).

claim: The externalization review places the harness as the stage where capability extends beyond prompt management into persistent infrastructure.
quote: The Harness layer-the topmost band in Figure 2 and the rightmost region in Figure 1 (lower panel)represents the current stage, in which capability extends beyond prompt management into persistent infrastructure.

claim: The code-harness survey describes planning as a control layer that decomposes tasks and coordinates multi-stage software workflows.
quote: Discussion: Planning for code generation can be understood as a core form of agentic harness: a control layer that organizes how an LLM agent decomposes tasks, grounds decisions in program structure, explores alternatives at inference time, and coordinates multi-stage software engineering workflows.

claim: On multi-agent orchestration, the code-harness survey reports that Anthropic's long-running harnesses separate planning, generation, and evaluation into distinct roles.
quote: Anthropic's long-running harnesses separate planning, generation, and evaluation into distinct roles, using structured artifacts and independent evaluation to maintain progress across long sessions [15,171].

claim: The TDD governance paper describes an orchestration engine that retains sole authority over workspace mutation.
quote: Unlike TDFlow-style autonomous execution, the orchestration engine retains sole authority over workspace mutation.
locator: sec. Proposed Approach and System Description, para 23

claim: For agentic RAG, the survey by its authors concludes that no single architecture is universally optimal and that effectiveness depends on aligning complexity with task requirements.
quote: The analysis demonstrates that no single architecture is universally optimal; effectiveness depends on aligning complexity with task requirements.

claim: The RAG-stack review says agentic and AutoRAG architectures combine AI agents with RAG pipelines for dynamic decision-making, self-optimization, and multi-agent coordination.
quote: Agentic and AutoRAG architectures are at the forefront of autonomous AI systems, combining AI agents with RAG pipelines to facilitate dynamic decision-making, self-optimization, and multi-agent coordination [73], [74].
locator: sec. Agentic and AutoRAG Architectures: Autonomous Optimization Systems, para 121

claim: The code-harness survey lists evaluation beyond final task success and consistent shared state across multiple agents among its open challenges.
quote: We further outline open challenges for harness engineering, including evaluation beyond final task success, verification under incomplete feedback, regression-free harness improvement, consistent shared state across multiple agents, human oversight for safety-critical actions, and extensions to multimodal environments.

claim: The agentic RAG survey likewise lists multi-agent coordination, process-aware evaluation, and governance as unresolved.
quote: Substantial open challenges remain in multi-agent coordination, process-aware evaluation, memory management, computational efficiency, and governance.

claim: The UniACE authors state that a reported score reflects a complete model–harness–environment configuration rather than the model alone.
quote: Agent benchmarks are increasingly used to compare large language models (LLMs) across domains, yet a reported score reflects a complete model--harness--environment configuration rather than the model alone.

claim: The harness-aware evaluation survey likewise reports that changing the execution system around a fixed model can alter performance and even reverse model rankings.
quote: As research pursues more general intelligence, recent results highlight the importance of the agent harness: changing the execution system around a fixed model can alter performance and even reverse model rankings.

claim: The Harness-Aware Evaluation survey reviews the development of agent harnesses and introduces a four-factor evaluation framework comprising the model, harness, environment, and evaluator, alongside the protocol under which they are tested.
quote: Yet inconsistent reporting of harness configurations, resource budgets, and scoring procedures makes benchmark results difficult to interpret and compare. This survey reviews the development of agent harnesses and introduces a four-factor evaluation framework comprising the model, harness, environment, and evaluator, alongside the protocol under which they are tested.

claim: UniACE reports that failure profiles are not only model-dependent but also task-dependent.
quote: While Section 4.5 presents the aggregated failure patterns across all advanced models, the following subsections examine how failure modes vary across different benchmark domains. These benchmark-specific analyses reveal that failure profiles are not only model-dependent but also task-dependent, with certain benchmarks exposing particular weaknesses in reasoning, parsing, or planning capabilities.
locator: sec. G Distribution of Failure Analysis for Each Benchmark, para 178

claim: The harness–post-training study observes that high ALFWorld success largely stems from harness-aware post-training in which a specific harness is fixed a priori.
quote: While existing post-training algorithms attain high success rates on ALFWorld (Feng et al., 2025), we observe that this performance largely stems from harness-aware post-training, where a specific harness is fixed a priori (Fig. 3).

claim: The coevolution survey describes a shifting boundary in which routine capability-bearing support migrates into model weights while constraint-bearing governance functions remain external.
quote: explaining the shifting functional boundary where routine capability-bearing support migrates inward into model weights while constraint-bearing governance functions remain external.

claim: The system-scaling paper argues that agent quality should be evaluated as a longitudinal systems property rather than a one-shot completion score.
quote: Agent quality should therefore be evaluated as a longitudinal systems property rather than a one-shot completion score.
locator: sec. From Single Episodes to Longitudinal Evaluation, para 45

claim: The Code as Agent Harness paper holds that a harness mutation should be treated like a code change to a safety-critical runtime.
quote: The central insight is that a harness mutation should be treated like a code change to a safety-critical runtime.
locator: sec. Self-Evolving Harnesses without Regression, para 216

claim: The externalization review observes that most evaluation logic today lives inside the model's chain of thought or in external benchmark harnesses that run post hoc.
quote: Most evaluation logic today lives either inside the model's chain of thought or in external benchmark harnesses that run post hoc.

claim: The agentic harness survey states that prompt engineering changes instructions and context engineering changes what evidence is presented to the model, while its harness-level view treats the operating environment as the object of analysis.
quote: Whereas prompt engineering changes instructions and context engineering changes what evidence is presented to the model, AHE treats the operating environment itself as the object of analysis, including tool schemas, planning artifacts, memory policies, retrieval strategies, sandbox configuration, verification sensors, permission tiers, routing rules, multiagent workflows, and human-review gates [281,178].
locator: sec. Agentic Harness Engineering for Adaptive Harness Optimization, para 96

claim: The Agentic Context Engineering paper defines context adaptation as modifying inputs with instructions, strategies, or evidence rather than weight updates.
quote: Large language model (LLM) applications such as agents and domain-specific reasoning increasingly rely on context adaptation: modifying inputs with instructions, strategies, or evidence, rather than weight updates.

claim: The oncology commentary frames context engineering as embedding models with the why behind institutional practices, clinician experience, and patient-specific nuances.
quote: If AI merely regurgitates one-size-fits-all recommendations, it replaces personalization with standardization, offering little more than an automated guideline. This commentary argues that the next leap forward for AI in oncology is “context engineering”: embedding models with the why behind institutional practices, clinician experience, and patient-specific nuances.

claim: The harness-aware evaluation survey reports that changing the execution system around a fixed model can alter performance and even reverse model rankings.
quote: As research pursues more general intelligence, recent results highlight the importance of the agent harness: changing the execution system around a fixed model can alter performance and even reverse model rankings.

claim: UniACE reports large bidirectional score changes and model-ranking reversals when compared with source implementations.
quote: Comparisons with source implementations show large bidirectional score changes and model-ranking reversals, while matched online and offline runs reveal substantial sensitivity to accessible evidence and its representation.

claim: The code-as-harness survey lists separating improvements in the harness from improvements in the base model as part of a research agenda.
quote: A practical research agenda includes: defining mutation operators for harness components; building telemetry standards; evaluating evolved harnesses across diverse tasks; enforcing safety invariants during evolution; and separating improvements in the harness from improvements in the base model.
locator: sec. Self-Evolving Harnesses without Regression, para 216

claim: The context-management study acknowledges the limitations of its synthetic, single-model, single-budget setup.
quote: We discuss the practical implications for agent framework design and the limitations of our synthetic, single-model, single-budget setup.

claim: The system-scaling paper notes that single-episode success still dominates reported metrics, leaving memory quality and context efficiency largely unmeasured.
quote: A growing line of work evaluates agents as systems through executable, multi-step benchmarks [16,23,46,24], alongside broader surveys of LLM-based agents [39] and catalogues of agentic safety threats [28]; yet single-episode success still dominates the reported metrics, leaving memory quality, context efficiency, communication fidelity, and safe evolution under repeated use largely unmeasured (we return to these in §5).
